questions.q: What is the PEEL structure for writing literature answers, and what does each letter stand for in the context of poetry analysis?
questions.a: PEEL stands for Point (main argument about the poem), Evidence (specific line/word from the text), Explanation (how the evidence creates meaning/effect), Link (connect back to theme/question). A wrong answer like "Point, Example, Explain, Conclusion" reveals the student memorizes acronyms without understanding the literary analysis purpose — "Link" specifically demands thematic connection, not just summary.

questions.q: A student writes: "कुकुआन के पहले दोहे में बादल बरसते हैं और मोर नाचते हैं जिससे विरहिणी को दुःख होता है।" Identify TWO specific weaknesses in this answer relative to CBSE marking expectations.
questions.a: Weakness 1: No direct textual evidence — the answer paraphrases generally instead of quoting "कजरि कजरि बरसत..." or "मोर नाचत...". Weakness 2: No analysis of POETIC DEVICE — it states WHAT happens but not HOW the imagery works (contrast, personification, sensory detail). A correct answer would name the device (विरोधाभास/contrast) and explain its emotional effect.

questions.q: Apply the PEEL structure to answer: "दूसरे दोहे में 'रात' और 'सुबह' के चक्र का क्या महत्व है?" Write a complete 4-sentence PEEL paragraph.
questions.a: Point: The night-dawn cycle symbolizes the endless waiting in virah. Evidence: "बहु बेरि बिताई रैन..." and "प्रभात भई..." show repeated nights passing. Explanation: Each "बहु बेरि" (many times) emphasizes duration; dawn brings no relief ("दुख न भागा"), making time itself an antagonist. Link: This temporal imagery reinforces bhakti as patient endurance — the devotee's wait mirrors the eternal night of separation. A wrong answer would merely translate lines without analyzing "बहु बेरि" as repetition device.

questions.q: Compare how the FIRST doha uses AUDITORY imagery (sound) versus the SECOND doha using VISUAL imagery (sight). Which creates a stronger sense of virah? Analyze with evidence.
questions.a: First doha: Auditory — "कजरि कजरि" (onomatopoeic rain sound), "मोर नाचत" implies peacock calls — sound amplifies the world's celebration, making silence of separation louder. Second doha: Visual — "रैन" (darkness), "प्रभात" (light), "नैन" (eyes) — sight emphasizes watching/waiting. Stronger: Auditory in first doha — sound is inescapable (rain falls everywhere), creating involuntary contrast; visual in second is voluntary (she watches), showing agency in devotion. Wrong answer: "Both are equal" — misses that auditory imagery creates IMMEDIATE sensory clash, while visual shows CHOSEN endurance.

questions.q: Evaluate this student claim: "कुकुआन की भाषा सरल ब्रजभाषा है इसलिए उनके दोहे समझने में आसान हैं।" Defend or refute using specific vocabulary from the text.
questions.a: Refute. The claim confuses "सरल" (simple) with "लोकप्रचलित" (colloquial). Text shows: "कजरि" (onomatopoeia), "विरह" (technical bhakti term), "बहु बेरि" (archaic multiplier), "नैन" (poetic eye), "प्रभात" (Sanskritized dawn). These require glossary support (as NCERT provides). The language is ACCESSIBLE but not SIMPLE — it uses precise poetic vocabulary (तत्सम/तद्भव mix) for emotional density. Wrong answer: "Yes it's simple" — reveals student equates familiar words with simple meaning, missing how कुकुआन compresses complex virah philosophy into deceptively plain words.

questions.q: Create a new 2-line doha in Braj Bhasha style that uses NATURE IMAGERY to express VIRAH, following कुकुआन's pattern of contrast. Explain your device choices.
questions.a: Example: "बसंत आयो वन फूले, कोयल बोले मधुर स्वर / विरहिन के अंग लगै शीत, जलत तन अंतर भीतर" — Device 1: Seasonal contrast (spring joy vs inner cold) like कुकुआन's monsoon. Device 2: Sound imagery (koel's sweet song) intensifying silence. Device 3: Internal/external body contrast ("अंग" vs "अंतर"). Good answer shows deliberate imitation of कुकुआन's structure: nature observation → personal application → philosophical link. Poor answer: generic sad lines without contrast or device awareness.
